data.one_liner: Utilities and classes for reading and writing byte buffers and binary data streams.
data.what_it_does: Provides ByteDataWriter and ByteDataReader classes to simplify reading and writing binary data formats. It allows working with byte sequences and streams efficiently, handling operations like reading/writing integers of various byte sizes and null-terminated byte sequences. It has zero external dependencies and runs on all Dart/Flutter platforms.
use_when: Building custom binary protocol decoders or encoders.
Reading and writing structured binary data to or from byte buffers incrementally.
Handling null-terminated bytes and variable-length integer byte streams.
avoid_when: Working only with text-based formats like JSON or XML.
Standard Dart typed_data ByteData methods are sufficient for your simple buffer operations.
strengths: Convenient sequential reader and writer APIs compared to manual index management with ByteData.
Cross-platform support across mobile, web, and desktop.
weaknesses: README documentation is very brief with only a single minimal example.
